# Results — Study 659 (Costless Collar)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**own SPY, buy a 5%-out-of-the-money put, sell a call whose premium exactly pays for the
put, and get equity upside with crash protection for free.** There is no live SPY option
chain in yfinance, so this is a **stylized Black-Scholes model**, not a real option-chain
backtest: every month the put is struck 5% below spot, and the call strike is solved so its
BS premium exactly matches the put's, both priced off trailing 63-day REALIZED volatility
(our proxy for implied vol — the approximation is named, not hidden). Offline & deterministic
once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30**
(the last complete calendar month). Fingerprint `44daf42aa058` (SPY).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily SPY raw OHLC + dividend-adjusted close (8,410 rows), 1993-02-01 → 2026-06-30 |
| Derived monthly sample | **397 months**, 1993-06-30 → 2026-06-30 (the first ~4 months are dropped: the 63-trading-day trailing-vol input needs a warm-up window before the first collar can be priced) |
| Model assumptions (named) | constant risk-free rate **3.0%/yr**; put struck **5% OTM**; call struck to make each month's premium exactly offset the put's, both priced Black-Scholes off **trailing 63-session realized vol** (5.6%–70.7% across the sample, mean 16.4%) — a **proxy for implied vol**, since no option chain exists in this study; both legs rolled monthly |
| Execution / costs | **one documented lag**: the vol input (and hence the floor/cap) for month *t* is measured through the close of month *t−1* — known before month *t* begins, zero look-ahead. Costs: 2 legs (put + call) × one-way cost × NAV, charged once per monthly roll; the equity leg is buy-and-hold (untraded, no cost) |
| Data quirks (named) | the modeled cap is **nearly vol-invariant** at this floor/tenor/rate (5.81%–6.67% across a 5.6%–70.7% vol range) — an emergent property of solving for equal BS premiums at short tenor and modest OTM%, not a coding error; see [`docs/references.md`](references.md) |

No survivorship on the Signal axis: SPY is an ETF tracking a fixed, rules-based index (S&P
500 committee reconstitution, not investor-driven attrition) and this study never conditions
on any current-membership panel.

## The headline — collar vs. SPY, full sample, cost-sensitivity

| cost (bps/leg) | mean(collar−SPY) | one-sample *t* | Newey-West(3) *t* | $1 → |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5.0 | −2.3 bps/mo | −0.34 | −0.33 | **$31.39** (SPY: $29.95) |
| 10.0 | −12.3 bps/mo | −1.79 | −1.76 | $21.17 |
| 15.0 | −22.3 bps/mo | **−3.25** | **−3.20** | $14.27 |
| 20.0 | −32.3 bps/mo | **−4.70** | **−4.63** | $9.62 |

**Break-even cost: 3.84 bps/leg.** Below it the modeled collar's *full-sample* average
return sits (insignificantly) above SPY's; above it, below — and by the desk's own
10 bps/leg convention the sign is already negative and *nearly* significant (*t* = −1.79).

## Where the floor bites — months SPY fell more than the put's own 5% strike

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| n | **37 / 397 months (9.3%)** |
| mean cushion (collar − SPY) | **+2.68 pts** |
| one-sample *t* | **+6.39** |
| worst SPY month | **−16.52%** |
| worst collar month (same month) | **−5.10%** |

## Where the cap bites — months SPY beat that month's modeled cap

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| n | **42 / 397 months (10.6%)** |
| mean cost (collar − SPY) | **−1.83 pts** |
| one-sample *t* | **−7.67** |
| best SPY month given up | **+12.70%** |

Both mechanisms are **individually decisive on the real tape** (|*t*| ≫ 2): the floor's
crash cushion is real, and the cap's cost is real. What's genuinely uncertain is which one
dominates over any given holding period.

## Terminal wealth, Sharpe and drawdown — full sample (net 5 bps)

| metric | SPY buy & hold | collar (net 5 bps) |
|---|--:|--:|
| $1 compounded, 1993-06-30 → 2026-06-30 | $29.95 | **$31.39** |
| Sharpe (excess of 3% cash) | 0.57 | **0.69** |
| max drawdown, full sample | **−50.8%** | −33.6% |

At the desk's low-cost assumption, the collar shows a **smoother ride, a higher Sharpe, and
even a slightly higher terminal wealth** than buy & hold — which is exactly the shape of the
"free lunch" the claim is selling. The next section is why we don't believe it's structural.

## Named crash windows — the exact events the claim is sold against

| window | SPY drawdown | collar drawdown | cut |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2008 GFC (2007-10-01 → 2009-03-31) | −50.8% | −31.9% | **−18.9 pts** |
| 2020 COVID (2020-01-01 → 2020-04-30) | −19.4% | −10.1% | **−9.4 pts** |

Real, substantial, mechanical drawdown protection in both headline crashes.

## Is the full-sample "edge" just 2 crash windows getting lucky?

Exclude **only** the two named windows above (22 of 397 months) — the 2000–2002 dot-com
bear market **stays in the sample**, so this isn't rigged to help SPY:

| metric | ex-2008/2020 (n=375) |
|---|--:|
| mean(collar − SPY) | **−10.8 bps/mo** |
| one-sample *t* | −1.95 |
| Newey-West(3) *t* | **−2.10** |
| $1 compounded over those 375 months | SPY **$61.05** vs. collar **$44.83** |
| Sharpe (excess of cash) | SPY 0.81 vs. collar 0.86 |

Outside the two windows the claim's own marketing invokes, the modeled collar **loses to
buy & hold by a HAC-robust, certifiable margin** (|*t*| ≥ 2, robust to the NW lag choice —
we checked 0/3/6/12 lags: −1.96 / −2.10 / −2.11 / −2.15) — a **27% relative shortfall in
terminal wealth** on the identical 375 months. The Sharpe ratio still edges out SPY (lower
volatility helps the ratio even when the compounded dollar outcome is worse — Sharpe is not
terminal wealth), but the number that actually pays your bills goes the other way. The
full-sample "free lunch" lives **entirely inside 22 months out of 397** — a favorable
realized-crash-timing draw, not a structural property of the trade.

## Synthetic positive control — the clip mechanics are unbiased

Deterministic monthly GBM total-return series (16%/yr vol, 9%/yr drift), no network, no
roll costs (isolating the pure clip effect from the flat cost assumption).

| world | result |
|---|---|
| null (floor=−99%, cap=+99% — cannot bind at 16%/yr synthetic vol), 20 seeds | diff ≡ **exactly zero** every month, every seed — 0/20 seeds show *any* deviation from raw SPY-like returns. The strongest possible non-signal (a *t*-ratio is undefined with zero variance — there is nothing to threshold) |
| planted (floor=−3%, cap=+2% — binds almost every month), 20 seeds | mean *t* = **−5.08** (sd 1.03), **|*t*| ≥ 2 in 20/20 seeds** |

The detector never invents an effect from a no-op band, and lights up unmistakably on a
tightly-binding planted one. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support
of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** Two mechanically real, individually decisive effects on the real tape:
  the floor cushions crashes (**+2.68 pts/event, *t* = +6.39**, worst month cut from −16.52%
  to −5.10%) and the cap costs bull months (**−1.83 pts/event, *t* = −7.67**, giving up as
  much as +12.70% in a single month). Which one nets out ahead is **regime-dependent, not a
  constant**: at low assumed costs and *with* the 2008/2020 crashes in the sample, the net
  effect is a statistical wash (*t* = −0.34); **excluding just those two named windows it
  flips to a certified, HAC-robust drag (NW *t* = −2.10)**. The claim isn't "wrong" about the
  mechanism — it's wrong that the sign is guaranteed.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The apparent full-sample edge survives only below a **3.84
  bps/leg** break-even — thinner than even the desk's own low-cost convention leaves room
  for, and far thinner than a realistic OTM SPX/SPY option bid-ask. By 10 bps/leg the sign is
  already negative and near-significant (*t* = −1.79); by 15 bps it's decisively negative
  (*t* = −3.25). And the entire full-sample "win" is concentrated in 22 of 397 months — a
  favorable realized-crash-timing draw that cannot be known in advance, not a structural
  edge that survives generic cost or timing stress.
- **"Truly free protection?" — BUSTED.** The cap's cost is real, significant, and mechanically
  guaranteed every time it binds (*t* = −7.67) — you always pay, whether or not a crash
  arrives to justify the payment. The full-sample "win" at low cost is a historical accident
  of two real crashes landing inside a 33-year sample, not a proof that the structure is
  free. "Costless" describes the option premium at inception; it does not describe the trade.
